title: Turn based game logic separated from rendering
when: A turn based game such as a board, tactics or card battle game needs its rules in a pure module that the interface only calls, so the rules can be tested in Node without a browser.
prompt:
Goal: The interface sends moves, the rules module returns new states, and node --test proves the rules.
Steps:
1. rules.mjs has no DOM, no timers and no Math.random; it exports initialState(options, rng), legalMoves(state), applyMove(state, move) and outcome(state) returning null, { winner } or { draw: true }.
2. State is plain JSON (players, board, currentPlayer, turn, log), so it can be saved, copied with structuredClone and compared.
3. applyMove checks that the move is in legalMoves(state) first; otherwise it returns { error: "illegal" } and changes nothing.
4. applyMove never mutates its input and returns a fresh object, which makes undo and replays trivial.
5. ui.js renders from state only and turns clicks or keys into move objects; animations read the move log, not hidden flags.
6. The computer opponent in ai.mjs scores legalMoves with an evaluation or a depth limited minimax, also pure.
7. test/rules.test.mjs uses node:test and node:assert/strict: opening state, each rule, illegal moves, win, draw and a replay of a recorded game.
Quality bar:
- Every rule written in the README has at least one test.
- Saving and loading mid game resumes identically.
Pitfalls:
- Rules hidden inside click handlers.
- Two sources of truth, DOM classes plus state.
- Tests that depend on a random setup without a fixed seed.
Verify:
- [ ] node --test passes with no browser.
- [ ] applyMove on a deep frozen state does not throw.
- [ ] An illegal move leaves the state deepEqual to before.
Output: rules.mjs, ai.mjs, ui.js and test/rules.test.mjs.

examples.input: separate the rules of my tactics game so I can test them
examples.output: pure rules.mjs with legalMoves and applyMove, state only UI, minimax ai, node --test suite
